question: According to the Commission’s official figures, the Directorate-General for Justice and Consumers has awarded around EUR 206 000 in European subsidies to the ‘Collectif contre l’islamophobie en Belgique’ (CIIB) for the MAGIC project. The Belgian State Security Service has, however, linked this organisation to the Muslim Brotherhood, an organisation that, according to a number of security services, aims to bring about the Islamisation of Western societies via subversive networks. 1.
Was the Commission aware of the link between the CIIB and the Muslim Brotherhood at the time the subsidy was awarded?
Was security screening carried out before awarding the funding?
Are there other EU-funded organisations that are linked to the Muslim Brotherhood or similar organisations?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.1.2026) The ‘Collectif pour l’Inclusion et contre l’Islamophobie en Belgique’ (CIIB) was a beneficiary of the MAGIC project with three other beneficiaries. The total funding of the project amounted to EUR 205,990 of which EUR 53,119 was allocated to CIIB. The grant agreement was signed on 14 December 2020 for a duration of 25 months starting on 1 March 2021.

The final payment took place in October 2023. CIIB has not been the beneficiary of any other grant since then. The checks performed on CIIB at selection and evaluation stage at the time of funding did not reveal any issue preventing the Commission from entering into a grant agreement with the organisation.

As elaborated in the Commission’s replies to written questions E-006476/20201 and E001741/20212, the Commission implements the mechanisms provided in the Financial Regulation3 for the award of funds. It carries out rigorous selection processes, including various checks on grant beneficiaries based on objective criteria such as the exclusion criteria or the EU restrictive measures.
Any entity that fails the test cannot be selected for funding.
